summary: Syed Ali Bilgrami (1853–1911) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Patna College, IIT Roorkee, Royal School of Mines, and the universities of Lucknow and London. He served the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and Cambridge (1901).

Syed Ameer Ali (1849–1928) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta (~1864–1868), where he later held a post from ~1873 to 1881.

Syed Hasan Askari (1901–1990) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College (~1920–1922), and Patna University (~1922–1924), he served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.
Syed Nawab Ali worked in history and archaeology. In 1932, he is attested as Professor of Persian at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and as Principal of Bahauddin College.
Sylvain Brocquet specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1980) and under Marie-Claude Porcher, and held a post at Aix-Marseille University.

Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. A Sorbonne student under Abel Bergaigne, he held chairs at EPHE (1885–1935), Collège de France (1890–1935), and directed the Maison Franco-Japonaise (1926–1928).

Sylvie Hureau works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts as maître de conférences at EPHE (attested 2012) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Sze-bong Tso specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Sámuel Brassai (1800–1897) worked in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at János Zsigmond Unitarian Highschool, he held professorships at John Sigismund Unitarian Academy (1837, 1858), Ludovika Military Academy (1848), and Franz Joseph University (1872–1884).

Sándor Kégl (1862–1920) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and Indologist. He earned his PhD at Eötvös Loránd University (~1884–1889) under Ignác Goldziher and Ármin Vámbéry, later serving there as PD of Persian (1893).

Sándor Kőrösi Csoma (1784–1842) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gábor College, Göttingen under Eichhorn and Fiorillo, and with Tibetan teachers Sangye Phuntsok and Kunga Cholek Dorje, later serving as Asiatic Society Librarian.
Søren Ludvig Tuxen (1850–1919) studied at Østre Borgerdyd school until 1868 and later held a post there in 1875.

Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Hammerich, Madvig, and Westergaard, receiving his PhD in 1883, and later served the university as Docent from 1899.
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako (1939–1988) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Path Press and served as an editor for the Buddhist Publication Society.
Sīlaratano studied under Narada Maha Thera, Nyanaponika Thera, and Ajahn Maha Bua (~1977–2011).

T. Chandrasekharan was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951), where he succeeded T. R. Chintamani.

T. Ganapati Sastri (1860–1926) was an Indologist who completed a doctorate at the University of Tübingen. From ~1908 to 1925, he served as Curator and Editor of the Travancore and Trivandrum Sanskrit series and Oriental Manuscripts Publications.

T. Griffith Foulk works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, taught there (~1987–1995), and later served as Riggs Professor of Religion at Sarah Lawrence College (~2012).
T. K. V. Desikachar (1938–2016) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (~1961–1989) and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

T. N. Ramachandran (1901–1973) was an Indologist and archaeologist. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1925–1934), and as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi (~1949–1954).
